author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the BRICS summit and a scheduled meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Indian television channels reported. It is Xi’s first visit to India in seven years and turns days of planning into a direct diplomatic test for Asia’s two most populous countries.

The leaders are expected to meet Saturday evening. Their talks come after a gradual effort to stabilize relations damaged by the 2020 border clash in the Himalayas, which killed 20 Indian soldiers and four Chinese troops. Xi and Modi have met twice in the past three years, but unresolved border and strategic tensions continue to shape the relationship.

The BRICS gathering provides a broader setting for discussions among major emerging economies, while the bilateral meeting offers a measure of whether recent contacts can produce practical progress. No outcome had been announced at the time of Xi’s arrival. Attention will center on the language used after the talks and whether the two governments identify concrete steps on border management, trade or diplomatic engagement.
dek: The Chinese president’s first visit to India in seven years moves a planned meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi from preparation to a closely watched diplomatic test.
headline: Xi arrives in Delhi for BRICS summit and Modi talks
